$comment: Golden vectors for the combat formulas (docs/formulas/combat.md).
The movement table and the torpedo-accuracy examples are quoted from the
original manual, so they check the implementation against the documented
game rather than against our own output. The starting squares come from
the rgbrcStart table in the binary and are confirmed by every one of the
161 tokens in the Exodus battle recordings.

movement_per_round.source: MANUAL.PDF p. 23-9 'Movement in Squares per Round'; DxyFromSpdRound in battle.c
movement_per_round.$comment: speed is the stored quarter-square index: 0 = 1/2 square per round, +1 = +1/4. Rounds are 0-based.

torpedo_accuracy.source: MANUAL.PDF p. 23-6 'Jammers' and 'Battle Computers'; CTorpHit in battle.c

cases.why: a plain 75% torpedo with nothing modifying it
a 50% battle computer halves the inaccuracy: 100 - (100-75)*0.5
two 30% computers combine to 51% (1 - 0.7*0.7) before this point: 100 - (100-75)*0.49
50% of jamming against 45% of computer leaves 5% of jamming
30% of jamming against 40% of computer leaves 10% of computer

start_squares.source: rgbrcStart at the start of the battle code segment
start_squares.$comment: Indexed as base = players*(players-1)/2, then the side index.

board_distance.$comment: Chebyshev distance: diagonals cost the same as orthogonals.
